h1:
Nonthaburi Food
You Have to Try Once
intro: Nonthaburi sits right next to Bangkok, just across the Chao Phraya River, yet its food has a strong character all its own. There are the krathon-bud fish cakes you can only really find on Koh Kret, century-old Mon dessert recipes passed down through generations, the famously pricey Nonthaburi durian, and decades-old shops around the Tha Nam Non riverside market. We've sorted out what to eat if you come to Nonthaburi, and where to go for it.

blocks.html: When people think of Nonthaburi food, two places come to mind first: Koh Kret and Tha Nam Non. These two areas are the heart of the local food scene. Koh Kret is an old Mon community that still makes sweets and dishes from original recipes, while Tha Nam Non is a market on the Chao Phraya with several shops that have been around for 40 years or more. We've split the food into four main groups so you can follow along and try them easily.

blocks.text: Krathon-Bud Fish Cakes, the Koh Kret Specialty

blocks.html: Krathon-bud fish cakes (tod mun nor kala) are something you can basically only find on Koh Kret. The krathon bud is a local plant in the same family as galangal that grows along the island's waterways. They chop it into small pieces and mix it into the fish-cake paste, so when you bite in you get a crunchy bit of the bud running through it, different from your usual fish cake. Walk onto the island and you'll find several fish-cake shops in a row, frying them fresh and hot right at the counter.

items.name: Nong Faed Krathon-Bud Fish Cakes, Koh Kret
items.blurb: One of the first shops many people hit as they walk onto the island. The fish cakes are soft, the krathon bud is crunchy, and the dip leans sweet. This is the best-reviewed name on the island.
items.meta: Koh Kret · under THB 100 per person

items.name: Khru Jiap Krathon-Bud Fish Cakes
items.blurb: Another spot people mention often. Fried fresh in every batch, sold in small or large sets, easy to snack on as you walk and graze.
items.meta: Koh Kret · small set THB 30, large set THB 50

items.name: Pa Bunrot Krathon-Bud Fish Cakes
items.blurb: A long-running shop that's been at it for ages, with a homey, old-school flavor. Good if you want the island's original recipe.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Krathon-bud fish cakes taste best hot. If you buy them to take home the crispness fades fast, so eat them at the shop or as you walk. Besides the fish cakes, these stalls usually sell fried flowers and fried vegetables alongside too. Worth a taste.

blocks.text: Mon Sweets and Royal-Style Thai Desserts

blocks.html: Koh Kret is a Mon community that picked up royal-court dessert recipes back in the reign of King Rama V. The story goes that palace cooks once called in villagers to help make sweets, and the knowledge has carried on to this day, to the point that there's a canal on the island people call the Sweets Canal. The desserts it's known for are things like thong yip, thong yot, foi thong, and rare auspicious sweets like ja mongkut, thong ek, and saneh chan.

items.name: Baan Ja Mongkut Thai Sweets
items.blurb: A shop for auspicious sweets in the Koh Kret community, with ja mongkut, thong ek, saneh chan, krachao sida, and dozens of other kinds. Good for souvenirs that come with a story.

items.name: Mae Phayom Sweets
items.blurb: Sells old-fashioned Thai sweets like khanom piak poon, kleeb lamduan, foi thong, thong yip, and thong yot. A name the Koh Kret locals pass along to each other.

blocks.html: Beyond the sweets, Koh Kret has plenty of other Mon dishes to try, like khao chae eaten cold in the hot season, and khanom jok or sweets wrapped in banana leaf that aren't too sugary. Walk the island's market on a weekend and you'll see vendors making things fresh in front of you.

Nonthaburi durian has to come up when you visit, because it's one of the most expensive durian varieties in Thailand. The flesh is fine and smooth with no stringiness, the skin is thin, the smell is fragrant rather than pungent, and the taste is gently sweet. The catch is that it only grows in certain areas along the Chao Phraya, and after the great flood of 2011 a lot of the old trees died, making the real thing hard to find and sending prices climbing. Real kan yao and Nonthaburi mon thong from some orchards are priced by the fruit, anywhere from a thousand to tens of thousands of THB.

items: Suan Ta Kan (Bang Krang) — a conservation learning center for native Nonthaburi durian with over 50 varieties, including kan yao, mon thong, and kop mae thao. Good for a look and to buy in season.
Suan Seri Nonthaburi Durian — a newer, larger orchard that takes bookings by round. Prices start in the high hundreds to low thousands of THB per kilo.
Timing — Nonthaburi durian comes out around April to June. If you want the real thing, book ahead and buy straight from the orchard.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Real Nonthaburi durian is expensive and scarce. If you spot a roadside stall selling it suspiciously cheap and claiming it's Nonthaburi durian, keep in mind it may well be durian from somewhere else. To be safe, buy from a well-known orchard and book by round.

blocks.text: Boat Noodles and Old-School Shops Around Tha Nam Non

blocks.html: Tha Nam Non is a riverside market on the Chao Phraya by the clock tower, with several long-running shops. Walk a few steps from the pier and you'll find food lined up: noodles, gui chai dumplings, som tam, and desserts. It's a place Nonthaburi locals have been coming to eat for generations.

items.name: Kuaytiao Mueang Non
items.blurb: An old pork-and-beef noodle shop that's a fixture of Tha Nam Non. The braised beef is soft and falling apart, the broth is fragrant, and it's cheap. Locals have been meeting up here to eat for years.
items.meta: Pracharat Road, Tha Nam Non · open 8:30am–5:00pm

items.name: Gui Chai 7 Si, Tha Nam Non
items.blurb: A steamed gui chai shop that's been selling for over 40 years, hand-shaped at the counter. The wrapper is thin and chewy, with colorful fillings in several styles. The line is packed almost all day.
items.meta: In front of the 7-Eleven near the clock tower · open 6:00am–7:00pm

items.name: Non Tam Laek
items.blurb: A well-known som tam and Isan food shop in the Tha Nam Non area, open for over 30 years. Bold, fully seasoned flavors. Good for people who like it spicy.
items.meta: Near the Tha Nam Non clock tower · som tam–Isan

items.name: Tiao Ruea Ko Baen Nai Suan
items.blurb: A boat-noodle spot with a café-like vibe and a riverside corner where you can dangle your feet and take photos. Has both beef and pork boat noodles, plus satay and grilled meatballs. Good for groups.

blocks.html: If you come to Tha Nam Non, aim for the morning to late morning, when all the shops are open and the food hasn't run out. You can graze shop by shop, then hop on a boat across to the other bank, or take a boat up to Koh Kret the same day.

blocks.text: Planning Your Nonthaburi Food Trip Without Missing Out

items: Weekdays vs. weekends — the Koh Kret market and dessert shops only really come alive on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. On weekdays many shops are closed. If you want to graze through everything, come on a weekend.
Getting there — for Tha Nam Non, take the MRT Purple Line or the Chao Phraya Express Boat. For Koh Kret, take the cross-river ferry from Wat Sanam Nuea pier in Pak Kret; the fare is just a few THB.
Bring cash — many shops in the market and on the island take cash mainly, so small bills will make life easier.

faq.q: What Nonthaburi food do I have to try?
faq.a: Koh Kret krathon-bud fish cakes are the specialty you can only find here. After that come the royal-style Mon desserts on Koh Kret, Nonthaburi durian in season, and the old-school shops around Tha Nam Non like Kuaytiao Mueang Non and Gui Chai 7 Si.

faq.q: Where's the best place to eat krathon-bud fish cakes?
faq.a: Walk onto Koh Kret and you'll find several krathon-bud fish-cake shops in a row. The most-reviewed names are Nong Faed, Khru Jiap, and Pa Bunrot. They fry fresh at the counter, and they taste best hot.

faq.q: Where do I buy real Nonthaburi durian, and how much is it?
faq.a: Real Nonthaburi durian is rare and pricey. Nonthaburi mon thong runs in the thousands of THB per kilo, and kan yao is far more than that. Some orchards sell by the fruit, from a thousand to tens of thousands of THB. We'd suggest buying from a known orchard like Suan Ta Kan or Suan Seri, and booking ahead between April and June.

faq.q: Is Koh Kret open every day?
faq.a: The market and shops on Koh Kret only really come alive on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. On weekdays many shops are closed or barely open. If you want to graze through everything, come on a weekend.

faq.q: How do I get to Tha Nam Non?
faq.a: You can reach Tha Nam Non by the MRT Purple Line or by the Chao Phraya Express Boat, which stops directly at Tha Nam Nonthaburi. From Tha Nam Non you can also catch a boat over to Koh Kret the same day.
